title: Fault-slice orchestra and root-cause storyboards for inference errors
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's runtime surfaces a wide range of inference failures (timeouts, backpressure/overload, model rejections, model-internal errors, and transport-level HTTP/gRPC codes). Teams need a single pane that both (a) classifies and groups error signals into actionable 'fault slices' and (b) provides narrative root-cause storyboards so engineers and oncall can quickly determine remediation actions and upstream ownership.

Goals:
- Produce a canonical failure ontology that normalizes signals from traces, metrics, and logs into a minimal set of fault slices (Timeout, Overload/Backpressure, ModelRejection, ModelRuntimeError, TransportError, ResourceExhaustion).
- Enrich trace hooks and the metrics/log pipeline so that each request emits a structured failure_reason label and contributing_tags (e.g. kernel_mismatch, kvcache_miss, oom, queue_time_high).
- Build a dashboard (Grafana + internal console pane) that surfaces: top fault slices by route/model, a request-flow Sankey that highlights where the failure surfaced (router → runtime → model → infra), a timeline of per-slice SLI exposure, and exemplar trace links + suggested remediation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tracehook enrichment: 95% of inference traces include failure_reason and at least one contributing_tag for failed requests in prod regions.
- Dashboard: queryable by customer_id, route_name, model_version, and time window. Must show aggregated SLI (success rate, p95 latency) per fault slice and list 10 representative traces per slice.
- Alerting: create at least two new SLO alerts (sustained increase in ModelRuntimeError rate; sudden spike in Overload errors) with runbook links.
- Migration: existing dashboards that currently break down by HTTP/gRPC code must map to the canonical slices and show mapping notes in the console.

Technical approach:
1) Failure ontology & mapping table: draft mapping in Confluence with deterministic rules (e.g., RPC deadline_exceeded => Timeout unless queue_time > 200ms then Overload). See doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Failure+Ontology+Draft.

2) Tracehook changes: add an enriched span attribute failure.reason and failure.tags[] in the tracehook library (runtime-agent v0.38). Instrumentation points: request_router, batching_loop, kernel_dispatch, model_inference, host_io. Keep payload small (string codes + short tag set). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1429.

3) Metrics/logs pipeline: update the OTel collector config to translate failure tags into metric labels and ensure Elastic/Kibana indexing uses normalized keyword fields. Add a small enrichment lambda to reconcile older traces that lack failure.reason.

4) Dashboard and UX: prototype in Grafana using PromQL for SLI and ES/KQL for trace lists; then port to Console pane with interactive drilldown and suggested runbook links. Prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/obs/fg-fault-slices.

5) Regression & QA: add unit tests for mapping table, integration test that simulates 5 failure types and asserts produced metrics/traces and Dashboard examples.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0 (design review): finalize mapping table and runbooks with PM/Design.
- Week 1 (instrumentation): land tracehook attributes behind a feature flag in runtime-agent; ship OTel config changes to staging.
- Week 2 (indexing + dashboards): deploy ES mapping changes; create Grafana prototype and console pane beta.
- Week 3 (canary): enable feature flag for 10% of traffic for one region; validate enrichment coverage and dashboard accuracy.
- Week 4 (full ops): remove feature flag, onboard SLO alerts, run a 48h observation window, and schedule follow-up retro.

Monitoring & metrics to validate success:
- fraction_enriched_traces = traces_with_failure_reason / total_failed_traces (target > 0.95)
- slice_distribution_change = KL divergence between baseline slice histogram and current (alert if > threshold)
- mean_diagnosis_time reduced by 30% (tracked via postmortem samples)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How granular should contributing_tags be? Too many tags will bloat metrics cardinality. Proposal: cap to 6 high-value tags and prioritize kernel/ordering/kvcache/oom/queue_time/quantization_mismatch.
- Mapping heuristics for borderline cases (e.g., deadline_exceeded vs queue-time-high): these are documented in the Confluence mapping rules but may need iterative tuning.

Next steps:
- Design review with PM (Lena) and Design (Marco) scheduled 2026-02-25.
- Land tracehook PR and a short-lived feature flag for alpha telemetry in staging.

Links to artifacts:

- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1429
- Grafana prototype: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/obs/fg-fault-slices
- Draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Fault+Slice+Runbooks
